| 2026-11-08 | MATCHING ON REAL DOCUMENTS AND AGAINST A VALUE-ONLY BASELINE. Corpus (`bench/sec_corpus.py`, `bench/sec_match_bench.py`): ten real quarterly earnings releases (Apple, Microsoft, Nvidia, Coca-Cola, PepsiCo, Johnson & Johnson, Procter & Gamble, Walmart, Home Depot, Costco; SEC EDGAR 8-K exhibit text and tables, converted to Word, 6,636 numbers) paired with the XBRL facts each company filed in its matching 10-Q (workbook, millions of dollars, all real). FIRST RUN found a precision defect: of 72 numbers the engine linked automatically, 11 were clearly wrong (15%), e.g. EPS "(0.01)" linked to "Increase in receivables", "7.3%" linked to Operating income, "3" linked to "Other income" via implicit thousands scaling, because short numbers matched large cells once scaled and long paragraphs lent every label a few words. FIXED in `match/engine.py` with three guards (a percentage never matches a scaled money cell; a short number matched only by implicit scaling goes to a person; in long paragraphs only the ~160 characters around the number count as its description), tests in `tests/test_match_guards.py`. A second rule was ADDED on evidence: a number of 5+ significant digits that fits exactly one source cell and whose text names part of that cell is accepted. RESULT NOW: of 6,636 numbers, 265 linked automatically, 2,433 sent to a person, 3,938 have no source cell (growth rates, per-share figures, dates, prose counts). PRECISION OF AUTOMATIC LINKS, judged by reading each against its row heading (one judge, me): 57 links before the new rule: 49 correct, 8 plausible but unverifiable (Walmart non-GAAP reconciliation tables), 0 wrong; 40 randomly sampled of the 207 links the new rule added: 40 correct (one ambiguous cash-flow row), 0 wrong. RECALL on numbers that are near-certainly linkable (4+ digits equal to a source value, 551): 247 linked automatically (45%), 304 sent to a person (55%), 0 missed. VALUE-ONLY BASELINE (link every number that has any source cell of the same value, as a script or the bundled skills would): that links 2,698 numbers; on a random 40 of the 2,433 Workroom sends to a person, about 6 are right, about 31 wrong, 3 unclear, so value-only precision there is about 15% and overall about 23% against Workroom automatic links at 0 wrong in 97 judged. COMPETITORS: none of the catalog rivals, nor office-desk, nor the bundled Office skill, links numbers to source cells at all (find and replace only); think-cell and UpSlide link by hand and were NOT run (closed, paid), so the value-only baseline stands in. Synthetic paraphrase benchmark after the change: 930 correct, 0 wrong, 0 decoys accepted (was 906 / 0 / 0). NOT verified: more than one judge; the 8 unverifiable Walmart links; the rest of the 2,433 sent to a person (only 40 read); other languages; messy documents that are not press releases (contracts, slide decks with charts); the HTML-to-Word conversion is mine, not the companies' own Word files | Tested (real filings, manual judging) | `bench/sec_corpus.py`, `bench/sec_match_bench.py` |
